'''''Crassula sarmentosa''''', commonly known as '''trailing jade plant''' and '''showy trailing jade''',<ref>{{cite book |last1=Witt |first1=Arne |title=Guide to the naturalized and invasive plants of Eastern Africa |date=2017 |isbn=978-1-78639-214-5 |page=302 |url=https://www.academia.edu/88722639/Guide_to_the_naturalized_and_invasive_plants_of_Eastern_Africa}}</ref> is a [[perennial]] [[succulent plant]] in the family ''[[Crassulaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite taxon |powo |id=273465-1 |title=''Crassula sarmentosa'' Harv. |access-date=November 27, 2024}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/Z7JK |title= Crassula sarmentosa Harv. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=November 27, 2024}}</ref> It is native to [[southern Africa]].<ref name="plantz">{{cite web |title=Crassula sarmentosa Harv. var. sarmentosa |work=[[South African National Biodiversity Institute]] |url=https://pza.sanbi.org/crassula-dejecta |access-date=2024-07-28}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Crassula sarmentosa var. sarmentosa 2019-12-13 6096.jpg|thumb|left|Green leaves with pale red edges]]
Featuring [[tubers]], the plant is irregularly shaped at the base of the stem, where it produces several, long, trailing branches up to 1 meter long, which rarely branch and mainly emanate from the base. The plant [[groundcover|forms a mat]], and can send out runners or [[stolon]]s, in addition to climbing or hanging from rocks.<ref name="plantz"/>

The evergreen leaves may or may not have a [[petiole (botany)|petiole]], up to 15 mm long, with a blade that varies from elliptic to ovate (usually ovate under the inflorescence and elliptic towards the base of the branches), acute or [[acuminate]], more or less sharply tapering towards the petiole, with an entire or [[serrate]] margin, with the margin flattened in the dorsiventral direction, green or yellowish-green, often with a red edge.<ref name="plantz"/> A [[variegated]] variety features green and cream striped leaves.

===Inflorescence===
The [[inflorescence]], which appear in winter through to spring, is a thyrsus ([[peduncle (botany)|stalked]]) with a rounded or flat top, on which the flowers are spread out at approximately right angles to each other. The [[calyx (botany)|calyx]] consists of linear-triangular [[petal]]s 1-3 mm long, sharp, naked, fleshy, green. The [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] is [[Trichome|stellate]], barely fused at the base, white or cream, sometimes with a red tint. [[Stamen]]s with anthers from white to pink.<ref name="plantz"/>

==Distribution==
[[Drought-tolerant]], the plant is generally found on the east coast of [[South Africa]], expanding from [[Knysna]] to the central parts of [[KwaZulu-Natal]], usually in rocky areas, ravines or canyons, in full sun or part shade.<ref name="plantz"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Crassula sarmentosa|work= World of Succulents |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/crassula-sarmentosa/ |access-date=2024-07-28}}</ref>
